content.title: Olympic Gold Medalist Scottie Scheffler and Meredith Scheffler’s Relationship Timeline
content.text: Dennis Rodman always had to stay sharp on the hardwood. Basketball moves fast. You either react or get burned. A five-time NBA champion, he built much of his Hall of Fame career on that split-second instinct.But there was one time he learned that unpredictability can show up off the court, too. It happened in 1997, when he pulled into the Chicago Bulls’ practice facility. Soon, he came face-to-face with someone he likely didn’t expect to ever meet.Family shockRodman’s chronic tardiness is well known, and it showed up that morning, too.The volatile power forward was late for the Bulls‘ shootaround. In a rush, he tried to make it through the gate at the Berto Center when, “out the blue, just like that,” as Dennis later recalled, a Black man sprinted up to his truck and began banging on the window.“I need to talk to you,” the man said, per ESPN. “I just want to let you know I’m your father.”Rodman — by then one of the best rebounders the game had ever seen — brushed him off.“Dude, I’m late for practice,” he remembered saying.A strange reaction? Not really, if you know the context.By then, Rodman was in his mid-30s. He’d grown up without a father and stopped expecting that to change — especially not from someone appearing out of nowhere claiming “the title.” To him, it felt like a hustle, and it couldn’t have come at a worse time.After all, the New Jersey native was already having a strange morning. This only made it worse. So all Dennis could think was, “Oh, come on, I gotta deal with this stuff today?”Related: Ex-Mavericks assistant on why Dennis Rodman had a separate locker room in Dallas: "He doesn't want to be in a room with the players"Rodman's first reaction was indifference“This stuff” wasn’t over, though. It came back later that night when the Bulls faced the Utah Jazz.Somewhere during the matchup, the same man showed up again, signing autographs and talking to reporters. During a timeout, Rodman looked up from the bench and saw him in the stands. Someone even asked him about it midgame. The two-time DPOY, however, still thought the whole thing was a “hoax.”Reporters, of course, saw it too. After the game, they crowded around Rodman. Did he know his father had been there? That the man claimed to be his dad had written a book about him? Rodman denied everything.“This guy came out of the blue, and I’ve never seen him before,” the Bulls legend later said.Rodman was right, at least partly. He hadn’t seen that man before. At least not since early childhood — a childhood spent in the Dallas projects, raised by a hardworking mother and two protective sisters.His real father had been gone for years. But on that strange day, the man at the gate and later inside the arena, Philander Rodman, really was his father.Why Philander chose that moment to show up wasn’t clear. One thing was clear, though. Dennis wasn’t his only child.“He had 16 wives and I think 29 kids. And I was his first one. Somebody told me that,” he said.At some point, Rodman realized it wasn’t a scam. Still, he couldn’t bring himself to care much.“I’m like, ‘Whatever.’ I was so used to not having a father after 37 years. I’m thinking, ‘You know, it’s a little late,’” he recalled.Late or not, they eventually reconnected.Their first real meeting came in the Philippines in 2012. A few years later, cancer took Philander. He passed away in 2020.Rodman, now a father of three — Alexis, D.J., and Trinity — followed a similar path in some ways. He was absent for much of their upbringing. But in 2024, the NBA icon found some closure, offering a public apology to his daughter, Trinity.Related: Michael Jordan was ready to save Dennis Rodman from losing everything: "He said he'd do anything to help"This story was originally published by Basketball Network on Apr 15, 2026, where it first appeared in the Off The Court section.
